candidate.answerReason: Since a-b>0, the condition (m-2)(a-b)<0 requires m-2<0. Thus m<2, choice B. At m=2, the strict inequality would fail.

methods.label: Identify the multiplier's sign
methods.explanation: When \(a>b\) becomes \((m-2)a<(m-2)b\), the inequality sign reverses, indicating multiplication by a negative number. Thus, \(m-2<0\), so \(m<2\).
methods.levelReason: Recognizing reversal under multiplication by a negative number is a Grade 7 inequality property.
